newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Formosa group '96 profit down, sales up.
newsitem.headline: Formosa group '96 profit down, sales up.

text.p: Formosa Plastics group, Taiwan's top private industrial conglomerate, said on Wednesday its 1996 pre-tax profits slid 19.03 percent, weighed down by a drop in product prices, while combined sales rose 3.0 percent.
The group's combined 1996 sales reached T$302.84 billion, up 3.0 percent from T$294.03 billion in 1995, a group spokesman told Reuters.

The group's combined 1996 pre-tax profits fell 19.03 percent to T$28.33 billion from 1995's T$34.99 billion. The drop was the group's biggest single-year profit decline in decades, the spokesman said by telephone.
"The profit decline was mainly caused by petrochemical and polyester fibre product price falls in 1996," he said.
The group has three key members: Formosa Plastics, Nan Ya Plastics and Formosa Chemical and Fiber. It has 14 other domestic affiliates and several overseas units.
Nan Ya, the group's top sales unit, had a 2.87 percent sales decline in 1996 to T$88.87 billion, with pretax profit down 5.43 percent to T$8.37 billion.
The group's combined overseas operations had total sales of T$77.68 billion, up 4.18 percent from 1995, but with combined pretax profits plunging 48.62 percent to T$4.85 billion.
The group launched its US$9 billion sixth naphtha cracker project in 1993 in central Taiwan.
Construction of the complex, including a naphtha cracker and oil refinery, is expected to take six years to complete.
